additions.metric: Earned coverage quality for the Month 4 proof launch

measurement.denominator: All eligible Month 4 earned coverage items published by third-party media, analysts, named experts, professional influencers or credible earned routes about The Stop Line proof launch or its press-release route during the launch reporting period, including positive, neutral, negative, high-quality, low-quality and proof-missing items.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude paid placements, owned posts, shared posts, unpublished drafts, internal mentions, duplicate syndications with no new editorial item, out-of-period items and coverage not tied to The Stop Line proof launch or press-release route. Do not exclude eligible coverage because it fails quality criteria, lacks proof citations, is unfavorable, or fails unrelated campaign governance or quality requirements.
measurement.numerator: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed quality threshold required by the registered source is recorded. Score each denominator item against the source-listed criteria: priority outlet or influencer, priority-audience relevance, key-message inclusion, positive or neutral tone, brand or spokesperson prominence, desired call to action and original reporting versus syndication; once the agreed threshold exists, count items meeting it.

additions.instrument: Partner-pack delivery register and distribution log

measurement.counted_event: Each partner proof pack delivery recorded during the measurement period when the pack is sent, published, handed over or otherwise made available to an intended referral partner, ecosystem partner or enterprise-buyer route, with observable evidence of the delivery event, period and recipient or channel scope.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude draft packs, prepared but undelivered packs, approvals, later downloads, later briefings, duplicate delivery records for the same pack delivery in the same instrument scope, failed sends, inaccessible links and deliveries of unrelated assets. Do not exclude eligible partner pack deliveries because the recipient did not download, attend a briefing, refer a lead or meet unrelated campaign quality requirements.

additions.metric: Influencer or creator committed-output delivery per creator
additions.instrument: Influencer and creator output commitment register

measurement.denominator: All influencer or creator output commitments recorded up front for eligible participating creators during the measurement period, using the source-listed target categories: one blog or long post; the selected committed number from the 3-5 social updates over about 14 days range; the selected committed number from the 2-3 posts per day live-challenge range for each eligible live-challenge day; and any other agreed committed pieces. If the source-required upfront commitment or selected value is not recorded for a creator or category, that creator-category aggregate is unavailable until recorded while the underlying criteria remain reported.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude draft, prepared or approved-but-unpublished pieces, duplicate captures of the same creator piece in the same platform scope, internal or test records, items outside the agreed measurement period, items not attributable to the eligible creator activation, and outputs outside the source-listed or up-front committed categories. Do not exclude eligible delivered output because later engagement, download, briefing, lead, sales-stage, approval, disclosure, proof-link, quality or unrelated campaign-governance requirements failed unless the registered source makes that later condition part of output delivery.
measurement.numerator: Denominator commitments whose matching creator output was sent, published or otherwise delivered by the eligible creator to the intended platform or channel during the agreed period, with observable evidence of creator identity, output type, publication or delivery time, platform or channel scope, and duplicate boundaries.

additions.instrument: Published-asset register and campaign distribution log

measurement.counted_event: Each campaign asset recorded as sent or published during the measurement period for The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, including proof pages, founder posts, partner material, technical proof stories, social-pack posts, earned outreach assets, employee advocacy posts, scorecards or approved toolkit assets when the register shows the asset reached its intended public, partner, employee, sales or owned-channel audience.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude drafts, prepared assets, approvals, internal-only review copies, duplicate publication records for the same asset in the same channel and period, failed sends or failed page loads, and records that cannot identify the asset and publication channel. Do not exclude eligible published assets because they later received no downloads, briefings, engagement, proof-page visits, meetings, leads or unrelated campaign-governance results.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts the unresolved public-profile conflict areas named by the source and keeps owner-awaiting unresolved items in scope.
judgments.quote: Each unresolved public-profile conflict area found in the Public-profile audit across founding year, headcount, address, legal name, domain identity or nearshore-price language, counted while the audited public source still carries the conflict without evidenced correction.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only approved proof assets with the required proof-type basis and excludes unapproved or duplicate assets.
judgments.quote: Each distinct approved proof asset in The Stop Line proof library with a recorded approval status and proof type marked as named reference, verifiable anonymous reference, technical artifact or internal demo; reference assets must also be traceable in the client-approved reference register.

judgments.reason: The denominator keeps all public AI claims in scope, while the numerator measures the required proof, owner, limit and approval evidence before release.
judgments.quote: Denominator claims that, before being sent or published, show approved proof, a senior owner, the stop line or stated limit, recorded claim-level and AI-language technical confirmation, and final sign-off for positioning, proof lane, claims and public references.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines a countable website visit/session tied to The Stop Line proof page and excludes only noneligible traffic or untied events.
judgments.quote: One website-analytics visit/session in which a visitor views The Stop Line proof page, with campaign tagging read from the required UTM fields where present.

judgments.reason: This is an instrument-defined analytics duration with clear page-load start and analytics/session end rules, so no open-case waiting rule is needed.
judgments.quote: The visitor leaves The Stop Line proof page, closes the session, becomes inactive according to the analytics session-timeout rule, or navigates to another page or tracked action.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts the specific proof-item open action on the proof page and excludes only invalid, duplicate or unrelated events.
judgments.quote: One tracked proof-item open on The Stop Line proof page, where a visitor expands, opens or otherwise inspects the proof behind an approved claim before any meeting request or AI-story acceptance step.

judgments.reason: The calculation gives observable criteria for a qualified meeting click without requiring a later meeting, lead, sale or reply outcome.
judgments.quote: One tracked event from The Stop Line proof page or a connected inbound route where website analytics or inbound-response records show a visitor clicked to request or book a meeting route intended for the named audiences and The Stop Line proof-page outcome. The click qualifies when the route is attributable to the page or campaign tagging, expresses meeting-request or booking intent, and is sent or published to the recipient system; it is not required to become an approved meeting, booked meeting, sales-qualified lead, completed sale or later reply.

judgments.reason: The ratio keeps all eligible public AI claims in the denominator and counts only those linked to approved proof with the required release evidence.
judgments.quote: Eligible public AI claims that, before release, show approved proof, a senior owner and the stop line or stated limit in the claim approval register and public-release checklist.

judgments.reason: The calculation preserves the source-required agreed enterprise-lead definition boundary and keeps the aggregate unavailable until that definition exists.
judgments.quote: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed enterprise-lead qualification definition required by the registered source is recorded. Once recorded, count each distinct lead record for a United States or European Union buyer that sales pipeline records confirm meets that agreed qualification definition and route-attribution records connect to The Stop Line before qualification through The Stop Line proof page, Signed by Humans founder content, partner proof pack or approved referral language.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines engaged visits as identifiable proof-page sessions with configured engagement events and avoids excluding eligible visits for unrelated campaign failures.
judgments.quote: One website analytics visit/session to The Stop Line proof page during the measurement period that records at least one configured proof-page engagement event, such as an analytics engaged-session event for that page, a proof-item open, or a qualified meeting click from that page.

judgments.reason: The calculation preserves the source-listed quality criteria and withholds the aggregate until the agreed threshold required by the source is recorded.
judgments.quote: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed quality threshold required by the registered source is recorded. Score each denominator item against the source-listed criteria: priority outlet or influencer, priority-audience relevance, key-message inclusion, positive or neutral tone, brand or spokesperson prominence, desired call to action and original reporting versus syndication; once the agreed threshold exists, count items meeting it.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures the preference split among owners exposed to both tested messages and keeps alternative or no-preference responses in scope.
judgments.quote: Sampled owners of midsize businesses in the Owner message test who were exposed to both the control-led message and the artificial-intelligence-capability alternative, both anchored in The Stop Line, and had an opportunity to record one message preference.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the owner comprehension population and the answer content required to count as correct.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator whose answer correctly explains that The Stop Line gives more control and visibility by showing approved proof, senior responsibility and the limit the system will not cross, without requiring the owner to become a technical buyer.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures trust movement using matched pre- and post-exposure readings and keeps flat or negative movement in the population.
judgments.quote: Sampled owners in the Owner message test with matched pre-exposure and post-exposure trust readings for The Stop Line in the same wave.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the post-exposure meeting-intent population and counts only positive next-meeting intent responses.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator who indicate positive intent after message exposure to take, request or accept a next meeting about The Stop Line or The B Team.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts coded reason-theme occurrences tied to valid message choices and keeps negative or alternative-message reasons eligible.
judgments.quote: Each coded theme occurrence recorded in the Owner message-test reason register from a respondent's submitted reason for choosing either tested message, tied to that respondent's valid message choice.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts platform-recorded reactions on approved founder launch content by founder and post in the read period.
judgments.quote: Reactions recorded by LinkedIn analytics or Substack analytics on approved Signed by Humans founder content published for the Month 5 founder launch post, counted by founder and post during the campaign read period.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts platform-recorded comments on approved founder launch content and does not exclude eligible comments for tone or quality.
judgments.quote: Exclude comments on unapproved content, non-founder content, content outside the Signed by Humans founder launch activity, duplicate analytics records, and comments not attributable to the measured post. Do not exclude negative, neutral, unanswered or low-quality eligible comments unless the analytics source identifies them as spam or platform-invalid.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts shares and saves only where the platform reports them, without treating unavailable saves as zero.
judgments.quote: Exclude unavailable metrics, unapproved content, non-founder content, content outside the Signed by Humans founder launch activity, duplicate analytics records, and shares or saves not attributable to the measured post. Do not treat unavailable saves as zero unless the source reports zero.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts proof-page clicks only when campaign tags connect them to approved founder content.
judgments.quote: Clicks from approved Signed by Humans founder content to the owned proof page, recorded in the website analytics report through the required campaign tags for the founder content route.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts partner reshares of approved launch or social-pack content and excludes materially altered or unrelated posts.
judgments.quote: Partner reshares of the approved Signed by Humans founder launch content or social-pack content, recorded in the social-pack reshare register during the Month 5 launch read period.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines qualified inbound conversations with observable audience, topic and attribution evidence, without requiring later sales or meeting outcomes.
judgments.quote: Each inbound conversation event in inbound-response records where an external contact from the card audience starts or replies in a conversation connected to approved Signed by Humans founder content by a tracked response, named post reference, tagged click path, reply, direct message, form source or other recorded campaign touchpoint. A conversation qualifies when the record shows observable audience eligibility, topic or intent relevant to Signed by Humans, The Stop Line, proof, senior responsibility, AI-supported delivery, referral, buyer interest or senior Sofia talent interest, and attributable evidence linking it to the founder content. Count the conversation itself; it does not need to become a sales-qualified lead, booked meeting, completed sale or approved follow-up.

judgments.reason: The calculation states the observed identities are platform account or recipient-record items, keeps platform counts separately usable and makes combined unique-person reach unavailable without a common identity method.
judgments.quote: Distinct platform identity items observed by the named analytics instrument as reached by the published Month 5 Signed by Humans founder launch post: LinkedIn account/profile reach deduplicated within LinkedIn for the measurement period, and Substack unique viewer, subscriber or recipient records deduplicated within Substack for the measurement period. Keep LinkedIn and Substack deduplicated platform counts separately usable; combined unique-person reach is unavailable unless a registered common-person identity method links records across platforms.

judgments.reason: The calculation supplies an observable 0-to-3 engagement-quality rubric that measures relevance, understanding and credible follow-up for founder launch engagement.
judgments.quote: Score each eligible engagement event on the founder launch post using the engagement-quality rubric: 0 points for passive or unclear engagement such as a reaction, save or unqualified click with no evident relevance; 1 point for a relevant proof-page click, share or comment showing basic attention to Signed by Humans, The Stop Line, proof or senior ownership; 2 points for an engaged comment, reshare or inbound conversation that reflects understanding of senior responsibility, approved proof or the stop line; 3 points for qualified buyer, partner or senior-talent engagement that asks a substantive question, repeats the proof-led message accurately, or creates a credible follow-up conversation. Eligible events include LinkedIn and Substack reactions, comments, shares, saves where available, proof-page clicks and qualified inbound conversations attributable to the founder launch post.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts completed tagged partner-pack downloads and excludes views, unrelated assets, tests and duplicate retries.
judgments.quote: A successful tagged analytics download event for the partner proof pack asset during the measurement period.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only partner briefings recorded as delivered through the required partner-proof content.
judgments.quote: A partner briefing for referral or ecosystem partners that is recorded in the completion register as delivered through its required partner-proof content.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines referred qualified leads through referral evidence, audience eligibility, source-record qualification status and sales-pipeline connection.
judgments.quote: Count each distinct lead that referral records and sales pipeline records identify as referred, enterprise-relevant, and connected to the partner proof pack or approved referral language before qualification. A referred qualified lead must have observable buyer eligibility for the named audience, topic or intent relevant to The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, attributable referral evidence, and a sales pipeline record showing the lead reached the campaign's qualified-lead status or equivalent qualifying stage used in the source records.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures partner-language claim-compliance checks as a percentage with failed and unresolved eligible checks kept in the denominator.
judgments.quote: All partner-language AI claim checks required for partner pack, briefing, release or referral language sent or published to partners during the measurement period.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts actual partner-pack delivery events with recipient or channel scope and excludes later downloads or briefings from the delivery count.
judgments.quote: Each partner proof pack delivery recorded during the measurement period when the pack is sent, published, handed over or otherwise made available to an intended referral partner, ecosystem partner or enterprise-buyer route, with observable evidence of the delivery event, period and recipient or channel scope.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts engagement events only when platform records establish the senior Sofia talent account or subscriber-record basis, without treating platform identities as cross-platform people.
judgments.quote: Each LinkedIn or Substack analytics-recorded engagement event during the monthly Month 6-Month 12 reporting window on Signed by Humans senior craft story content, counted only when the same platform's analytics, account metadata or subscriber record identifies the acting account or subscriber record as senior Sofia talent: Sofia location or Sofia-attributable recruitment source, senior-level engineering or technical role, and content engagement tied to the craft story asset. Qualifying engagement events include LinkedIn reactions, comments, shares and saves where available, and Substack clicks, likes, comments, replies or comparable analytics events tied to the asset.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts LinkedIn profile visits attributable to senior-talent routes and excludes visits without observable talent-route attribution.
judgments.quote: Each LinkedIn profile visit recorded during the monthly reporting window that is attributable in the LinkedIn analytics report to a senior-talent route, such as the senior craft story series, talent-facing post route, campaign tag or referral path.

judgments.reason: The calculation uses applicant, referral or recruitment records to count distinct people with senior Sofia qualification, candidate interest and campaign-asset ties.
judgments.quote: Each distinct person from the Sofia senior-engineering talent audience who shows candidate interest through an application, referral, direct inbound message or recruitment-review record, and whose record evidences both senior-engineering qualification and a tie to approved The Stop Line or Signed by Humans story assets.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts defined buyer engagement actions tied to craft-linked proof and does not require later meetings or leads.
judgments.quote: Each buyer engagement action during the monthly reporting window tied to craft-linked proof, including an engaged proof-page visit, proof-item open, qualified meeting click, or inbound buyer response connected to a Signed by Humans craft story, The Stop Line proof page, approved proof item or tagged campaign path. A response qualifies when the message or form submission is sent or published to its recipient, not when prepared or approved.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts proof-page clicks only when campaign tags or equivalent source-path evidence ties them to senior craft stories.
judgments.quote: Each website analytics click event from a Signed by Humans senior craft story to The Stop Line proof page or a proof-page item, identified by campaign tags, UTM fields or equivalent source-path evidence for the craft story asset.

judgments.reason: The response-time calculation uses a reporting cutoff, completed-response count and separate still-open elapsed ages without mixing open ages into the mean.
judgments.quote: For each reporting read, use the stated reporting cutoff timestamp and calculate mean hours only for eligible conversation items whose first response was sent or published to the recipient by that cutoff; report the completed-response count used. Escalation, preparation, approval, routing, administrative handoff or the reporting cutoff itself does not stop the clock. If no eligible items have a completed response by the cutoff, report the mean as unavailable.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts issues only when recorded as resolved with evidence through approved answer routes, while unresolved eligible issues remain visible in the register.
judgments.quote: Distinct eligible AI-trust, governance, proof, buyer-risk or claim-boundary issue recorded in the triage register as resolved with evidence, using an approved answer route that keeps the response inside approved proof, senior responsibility and stated limits.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures consistency over all eligible sent or published messages and keeps inconsistent or challenged messages in the denominator.
judgments.quote: All eligible sent or published Conversation Management responses and Observatory newsroom messages in the period that address The Stop Line, Signed by Humans, AI trust, governance, proof, buyer risk or public AI claims.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts sent or published responses that reuse a recorded approved answer source and excludes drafts or unsent responses.
judgments.quote: Each sent or published eligible response or newsroom message that reuses an approved answer from the approved answer set, Q&A/FAQ or Key-Message Table, with the approved answer source recorded in the reuse register.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts recorded senior escalations triggered by the named crisis-tripwire categories before publication.
judgments.quote: Each recorded escalation sent to a senior person before publication because an eligible issue triggered a litigation, disclosure, deal, restructuring, life-safety or regulatory crisis tripwire.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures the share of sampled technical buyers who say the proof gives enough evidence for a next meeting.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator who say The Stop Line gives enough evidence to take a next meeting.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts analytics views of technical proof-story assets and excludes unrelated or untagged content.
judgments.quote: Website analytics events recording a view of technical proof-story artifact content under The Stop Line, including technical artifacts, architecture notes, approved demos, proof labels or related technical proof assets.

judgments.reason: This is an instrument-defined analytics duration with tagged technical-content start and analytics engaged-time end rules.
judgments.quote: The visitor exits, closes, navigates away from or becomes inactive on the tagged technical proof content session according to the analytics tool's engaged-time rule.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only buyer-facing sales use events and excludes internal preparation, approvals and duplicate use records.
judgments.quote: A recorded sales use of the technical proof story in a buyer-facing sales context, such as sending, presenting or publishing the story to a prospect or using it in a qualified sales conversation.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines qualified technical conversations by participant eligibility, proof-related topic or intent and attributable touchpoint evidence.
judgments.quote: Count each distinct completed conversation event in inbound-response records or sales pipeline records where an external technical buyer, including a CTO, architecture owner or comparable technical decision or influence role, discusses The Stop Line technical proof story or approved proof assets. A conversation qualifies when the record shows audience eligibility, topic or intent tied to technical proof of AI-supported delivery, senior ownership, claim limits or proof assets, and attribution to the technical proof story or approved proof assets through a recorded touchpoint, reply, message thread, form source, meeting note or tagged campaign path.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts earned briefings only after the eligible recipient or representative confirms or accepts the briefing.
judgments.quote: An earned outreach briefing secured in Month 10: a proof-led briefing about The Stop Line with a journalist, analyst, named expert, professional influencer or credible third-party route, recorded after the eligible recipient or representative confirms the briefing or accepts the briefing invitation.

judgments.reason: The calculation preserves the source-listed quality criteria and makes the aggregate unavailable until the agreed quality threshold is recorded.
judgments.quote: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed quality threshold is recorded in the registered sources. Score each denominator item against the source-listed criteria: priority outlet/influencer, priority-audience relevance, key-message inclusion, positive or neutral tone, brand/spokesperson prominence, desired call to action and original reporting vs syndication; once the agreed threshold exists, count items meeting it.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts proof citations by distinct cited proof source or proof type within eligible earned coverage items.
judgments.quote: A proof citation in earned coverage: one recorded instance in an eligible published earned coverage item where the coverage explicitly cites, links to, quotes or names an approved The Stop Line proof source or proof type, including the proof page, proof library asset, named reference, verifiable anonymous reference, technical artifact, internal demo, senior owner or stated limit. Count one citation per coverage item per distinct cited proof source or proof type.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines qualified inbound conversation threads after earned exposure without requiring later sales follow-up, booked meetings or lead status.
judgments.quote: One distinct inbound conversation thread recorded in inbound-response records and/or sales pipeline records where an eligible external contact in the card audience, meaning a professional influencer, journalist, analyst, named expert or enterprise buyer reached through credible third parties, sends an inbound enquiry or reply after traceable earned exposure to The Stop Line. For this operational calculation, the thread qualifies when the record shows all of: observable audience eligibility; topic or intent tied to The Stop Line proof, proof-led earned coverage, expert discussion, partner or referral opportunity, or enterprise-buyer interest; attributable earned-exposure evidence before the inbound message; and enough recorded thread evidence to distinguish it from duplicates and irrelevant events. Count the conversation thread, not later lead qualification, booked meetings, sales follow-up, sales-qualified status, coverage publication or reporting completion.

judgments.reason: The calculation uses the source-listed creator-output target categories and makes creator-category aggregates unavailable when the required upfront commitment is not recorded.
judgments.quote: All influencer or creator output commitments recorded up front for eligible participating creators during the measurement period, using the source-listed target categories: one blog or long post; the selected committed number from the 3-5 social updates over about 14 days range; the selected committed number from the 2-3 posts per day live-challenge range for each eligible live-challenge day; and any other agreed committed pieces. If the source-required upfront commitment or selected value is not recorded for a creator or category, that creator-category aggregate is unavailable until recorded while the underlying criteria remain reported.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts distinct registered advocate people only after a sent or published advocacy action, not after training or approval alone.
judgments.quote: Each registered employee advocate or approved supporter advocate who, after Conversation Management training, sends or publishes at least one Month 11 Signed by Humans advocacy post or share using the provided language or proof link.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the post-quality population and counts published posts that stay within approved language, proof boundaries and escalation rules.
judgments.quote: Published denominator posts that stay inside approved Signed by Humans language, include approved proof links where the post makes a claim, preserve the proof boundary and do-not-say lines, and route questions the advocate should not answer themselves to escalation rather than inventing claims.

judgments.reason: The calculation supplies a 0-to-3 engagement-quality rubric with observable anchors tied to advocacy relevance, proof, limits and follow-up quality.
judgments.quote: Score each eligible LinkedIn analytics or inbound-response engagement action tied to a Month 11 advocate post from 0 to 3 points: 0 = irrelevant, spam-like, hostile without substantive issue, or unrelated to The Stop Line or Signed by Humans; 1 = minimal acknowledgement such as a reaction or generic share with no readable substance; 2 = relevant engagement with readable attention to the post, proof link, senior craft, approved proof boundary, or do-not-say lines, including substantive comments, reposts or saves where available; 3 = high-quality engagement that advances the intended advocacy outcome, such as a substantive comment, repost, share, proof-page click-through, or inbound response that is attributable to the advocate post and engages with approved proof, senior responsibility, limits, or escalation instead of creating unapproved AI claims. Qualified inbound responses are counted only when the named inbound-response record shows observable audience eligibility, topic or intent relevant to The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, attributable event evidence tying it to the post, and duplicate or irrelevant-event exclusions; do not require budget, purchasing authority, sales stage, booked meeting, sale, or later sales qualification unless the source makes that later event part of this named outcome.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts proof-page clicks only when campaign identifiers or UTM tags attribute them to Month 11 advocate posts.
judgments.quote: Each website analytics click event landing on the approved proof page from a Month 11 advocate post with the required campaign identifier or UTM tags for the employee advocacy push.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts logged escalations from advocate questions for proof, claims, technical, legal, disclosure, crisis or approval issues the advocate should not answer.
judgments.quote: Each logged escalation from an advocate question in the Month 11 employee advocacy push where the advocate uses the Conversation Management route for a proof, claim, do-not-say, technical, legal, disclosure, crisis-tripwire, or approval question they should not answer themselves.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts scorecard completion only when the after-campaign executive scorecard is produced within the source reporting window.
judgments.quote: Executive scorecard completion recorded when the Month 12 one-page after-campaign executive scorecard is produced within ten working days of the final campaign reading.

judgments.reason: The calculation keeps all required headline KPIs in the denominator and counts only those reporting baseline, target, result and trend together.
judgments.quote: Required headline KPIs that appear on the one-page executive scorecard and show readable baseline, target, result and trend fields together. A baseline or target that the registered source says is not yet established qualifies only if it is explicitly labelled that way and carries the named first-read or decision point required by the source.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only Key-Message Table changes approved after measurement review with evidence, date and approval record.
judgments.quote: Key-Message Table message change approved after the measurement review, where the register shows the changed message, supporting evidence or proof gap, review date and approval record.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts next-year proof gaps only when the missing proof, affected claim or message and Month 12 evidence are recorded.
judgments.quote: Next-year proof gap named in the proof-gap register, with the missing proof, affected claim or message, and the evidence from Month 12 measurement that establishes the gap.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts quarter-end contribution review completion only when the evaluation narrative addresses enterprise-lead contribution for the quarter.
judgments.quote: Quarter-end enterprise-lead contribution review completed when the quarter-end evaluation narrative records whether The Stop Line and Signed by Humans contributed to the enterprise-lead target using the quarter-end review evidence.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts campaign assets only after they are sent or published to their intended audience, excluding drafts, approvals and failed sends.
judgments.quote: Each campaign asset recorded as sent or published during the measurement period for The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, including proof pages, founder posts, partner material, technical proof stories, social-pack posts, earned outreach assets, employee advocacy posts, scorecards or approved toolkit assets when the register shows the asset reached its intended public, partner, employee, sales or owned-channel audience.
